_about: Languages, runtimes and execution targets. A separate axis from concepts — a property of where an implementation's code can run, not of the idea it implements.

technologies.name: JavaScript / TypeScript
technologies.note: Runs in the browser and in Node. The default for anything that has to be seen in a page.

technologies.name: Python
technologies.note: Where the scientific, solver and ML stacks live. Not a browser target.

technologies.name: C / C++
technologies.note: Where the fast reference implementations usually are; reachable from elsewhere via bindings or WASM.

technologies.name: Rust
technologies.note: Increasingly the source language for WASM-targeted generation code.

technologies.name: C#
technologies.note: Unity's language; a large share of shipped game PCG is written here.

technologies.name: GLSL / WGSL
technologies.note: Shader languages. Per-pixel generation, no CPU readback.

technologies.name: Node
technologies.note: Server-side JavaScript. No GPU or DOM without extra work.

technologies.name: Browser
technologies.note: Canvas, WebGL, WebGPU, Web Audio. The only runtime that can both generate and display.

technologies.name: WebAssembly
technologies.note: How C++/Rust implementations reach the browser and Node.

technologies.name: GPU
technologies.note: Massively parallel, hard to read back from, and invisible to gameplay logic on the CPU.

technologies.name: Native / desktop
technologies.note: Where offline simulation and baking happen when the budget is minutes rather than milliseconds.
